clue.text: Round and plump and booming

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
rotund means plump or chubby

explanation.surface: A description of someone fat, rounded and loud, like a jolly opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'and' reads as part of a list of adjectives, but it only joins wordplay to wordplay; the second joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orotund voice is full, resonant and loud, a booming sound.

clue.text: Where one may see one on a Malibu board at a very successful point?

definitions.text: Where one may see one on a Malibu board
definitions.meaning: surface reading: a surfer riding a board at the famous Californian beach, up on top of the water
setter's reading: the idiom for being at the height of success

explanation.surface: A picture of a surfer at Malibu, perched up high on a breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfing picture is literal: a surfer stands atop the swell. The same phrase is the idiom for riding high in life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone enjoying a peak of success, as a surfer is lifted to the top of the swell.

clue.text: See 1 down
Overcoat carried by Paul's Terence

indicators.note: what is carried is held within, so the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two names

explanation.surface: Terence, who belongs to Paul, is wearing an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanning PaUL'S TERence gives ULSTER; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, originally made in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Unusually sound sleep for Eliot inside? A measure

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the poet T. S. Eliot, reduced to his initials
surface padding: it only says the initials join the mix

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dose of something to give the poet Eliot a good night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' only says Eliot's initials go into the mix with the other letters; the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessertspoonful is a standard kitchen quantity, used as a unit when measuring medicine or ingredients.

clue.text: Glib talk by son in shower

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
patter is the slick talk of a salesman

explanation.surface: A son chatters away smoothly while taking a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside, so the son's letter sits next to the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatter is a light sprinkling of drops, a small shower.

clue.text: Impending disaster in classroom, odd few suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy, not what it seems, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher fears trouble from a few strange pupils in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Greek story Damocles sat at a feast beneath a sword hung by a single hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for a threat hanging over someone that may fall at any moment.

clue.text: A friend netting 1m causes bitterness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it inside, so one piece is caught within another

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal
the digit 1 as the letter I, and M for metre or million

explanation.surface: A friend who scoops a million leads to resentment among the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 is read as Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill feeling, a synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Infant, led, trod awkwardly

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means doing it clumsily, so the letters stumble out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small child, led by the hand, walks clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a near &lit picture: an infant learning to walk does tread awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a young child just learning to walk, an infant in everyday speech.

clue.text: Arab up in bedsit?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a Moor is a North African Muslim, loosely equated with an Arab

explanation.surface: An Arab gentleman is staying up late in a rented bedsit.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British single rented room used for both sleeping and living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single room, so the answer describes it, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Portable we hear?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: something easy to carry, perhaps a laptop or television
setter's reading: a carried device whose output we listen to, not one we watch

explanation.surface: A question about something carried around that we can pick up by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but there is no sound-alike: it simply says the portable is listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A small battery set built with transistors was the classic portable device for listening to broadcasts.

clue.text: Display stand in entrance written about before

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
ere is the old word for before

explanation.surface: A display stand placed in the entrance hall, with something written on it previously.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for entrance is written backwards, then the archaic 'before' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a set of open shelves for displaying ornaments, a type of display stand.

clue.text: Part of old implement's in hollow

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A piece of an antique tool lies in a hollow in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is olD IMPLEment; the 's is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small hollow or dent, in the cheek or on a surface.

clue.text: King muttered drunkenly about learner's instrument

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round another piece
someone acting drunkenly lurches about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
L is for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A tipsy king mumbles about a beginner's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum is a timpani, a large drum with a bowl-shaped body played in orchestras.

clue.text: Lively dance in part of film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fast Scottish or Irish folk dance
second meaning: a spool of cinema film, one section of a movie

explanation.surface: A spirited dance appears in a scene of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brisk Celtic folk dance and a spool on which a section of film is wound.

clue.text: Man's name sure flummoxed hospital worker

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: someone flummoxed is confused, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's name, says someone sure of it, baffles a member of hospital staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to man; the 's simply attaches it to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified nurse on a hospital ward, ranking below a sister.

clue.text: Italian boy in Spanish city, on wrong road

indicators.note: something wrong is not correct, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: León is a city in north-west Spain
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian lad in a Spanish city has taken the wrong road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the city before the rest, as in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo is an Italian given name for a boy, as borne by Leonardo da Vinci.

clue.text: Vet slack script

parts.note: to vet someone is to screen or check them
play is looseness or give in a rope or mechanism

explanation.surface: An instruction to check a sloppily written script.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Vet' and 'slack' look like adjective and verb about the script, but each is a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written script for a film.

clue.text: Breeding colony of birds in castle on English lines

parts.note: the rook is the castle piece in chess
E is the abbreviation for English
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: Birds nesting together in a castle built in the English style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the castle before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of nesting rooks, and by extension of other birds or seals.

clue.text: Wife behind signal flag

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
aft is the nautical word for behind or at the rear

explanation.surface: A wife stands behind a flag being waved as a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word placing the wife, but it is a letter-giver in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: In naval usage a waft is a flag or pennant hoisted as a signal.

clue.text: Wally, for example, has first-rate weapon

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a fool, an ass
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Wally, a named man, owns a top-quality weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally looks like a name, but here it is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender spear used by southern African peoples, a weapon.

clue.text: Iron Lady's hat?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A question about headwear worn by the Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' points at Thatcher, but the two words split: the metal's symbol plus a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim.

clue.text: Supported ring in Pacific island

parts.note: borne means carried or supported
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone is held up by a ring buoy off a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia, on the western edge of the Pacific region.

clue.text: Supervise extra watch

parts.note: over means extra or left over, as in surplus
to see is to watch

explanation.surface: A manager is told to supervise an additional shift on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise work or workers, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Stage favourites turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a teacher's pets are favourites

explanation.surface: Popular performers arrive at the theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks like a theatre, but it is a stage in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a process or sequence.

clue.text: Skilful pickpocket right inside dreadul dreadful ghetto

parts.note: surface padding: a stray misspelt duplicate in the source text, to be ignored

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one letter goes into the middle of the rest
dreadful means terrible, so the following letters are badly mangled

parts.note: taken as written; the anagram word doubles as fodder
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A skilled thief does well inside a grim slum.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints a stray 'dreadul' before 'dreadful'; ignore it. 'dreadful' is both signal and part of the letters. The Artful Dodger is the boy pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is Fagin's most adept young thief in Oliver Twist, the archetypal skilful pickpocket.

clue.text: Scottish town put in register a list of employees and their wages

definitions.text: a list of employees and their wages

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so the town goes within

parts.note: a poll is a register of voters or names
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish town is entered on a list of employees and their pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A payroll is a company's record of staff and the pay owed to each.

clue.text: Must aid ground such as Wembley?

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are pounded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An appeal to help a football ground like Wembley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as a football ground, fitting Wembley, but it signals the shuffle. Wembley is England's national football venue in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley is an example of a stadium, a large sports arena; the question mark flags definition by example.
